title: ShortPath SDK playbook + experiments notebook
content:
Context and intent:
This is a lightweight, low-friction playbook for the ShortPath SDK: a stripped-down developer experience intended to get an engineer from zero to an instrumented sample app in ~15 minutes. Purpose is to prototype quick onboarding heuristics, telemetry contract experiments, and a small set of deterministic smoke scenarios we call "scavenger tests".

Why ShortPath?
- We want a mini-quickstart with very small cognitive load for curious engineers (not the full product tour).
- Probes feature toggles that later inform larger SDK defaults (batching, warmup, stub-mode).
- Captures empirical data for Optimize team: which quick tweaks yield the largest drop in median time-to-success.

Target persona:
- Backend engineer (familiar with Node/Python) wanting to add a single LLM endpoint for an internal tool.
- Time budget: 10–30 minutes.
- Needs: minimal deps, local dev loop, deterministic test harness, basic observability.

Success criteria (experiments):
- 80% of test users complete the sample flow in <= 15 minutes without reading docs.
- Quickstart produces a working generation with streaming and error fallback.
- Telemetry emitted for: init, first request latency, fallback trigger, and cache hit/miss.

Core flow (15-min path):
1) Install: npm/pip one-liner (zero config, uses REDWOOD_API_KEY if set)
2) Run local stub mode: shortpath-run --sample-app (starts fake runtime, logs verbose)
3) Copy sample prompt/template, call generate() to produce a response stream
4) Observe telemetry in local UI or console (basic counts)
5) Swap to hosted mode with one env var (REDWOOD_ENV=hosted) and re-run
6) Validate fallback by toggling SHORTPATH_FORCE_FALLBACK=1

Quick CLI snippets (for README):
- Node install + run:
  npm install @redwood/shortpath && npx shortpath-run --sample-app
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
  node examples/simple-generate.js

- Python minimal:
  pip install redwood-shortpath
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
  python examples/simple_generate.py

Scavenger tests (deterministic sanity suite):
- S1: Local stub returns predictable token stream for prompt "hello world"
- S2: Fallback chain triggers when stub returns 503; app must still return a 200 with fallback flag
- S3: KV prefix cache returns cached completion on repeated identical prompt
- S4: Telemetry contains request_id and latency_ms <= 200ms in stub mode
(Each test has a single assertion and runs in < 1s locally.)

Telemetry contract (minimal):
- init: { sdk_version, runtime_mode, env }
- request: { request_id, model, seq_len_estimate, start_ts }
- response_complete: { request_id, end_ts, tokens_emitted, fallback_used }
- error: { request_id, error_code, upstream_model }
Sampling rules: default 10% for dev accounts, 100% when REDWOOD_DEBUG=1

Developer-facing docs structure (short doc outline)
- 1) TL;DR: three commands to get a streaming reply
- 2) Concepts: stub mode, hosted switch, fallback policy, cassette snapshots
- 3) Quick API surface: generate(), stream(), embed(), run_locally()
- 4) Scavenger tests & how to run them
- 5) Troubleshooting: common failure modes and remedies

Cassette snapshotting (experimental):
- shortpath-run can record a "cassette" for the first 10 requests. These are compact JSON files (prompt, kv-cache-keys, token fragments) that can be replayed by CI.
- Use: SHORTPATH_RECORD=1 npm test -> generates cassettes/ in repo; CI can replay with SHORTPATH_REPLAY=1 to ensure regressions are caught.

Local hermetic runner: shortpath-run
- Goals: fast startup (<1s), deterministic responses, simple HTTP port 8085 with minimal routes: /generate, /stream, /health, /admin/replay
- Exposes verbose logs for the scavenger tests to assert on request ids and telemetry events.

Edge & failure modes (notes for UX copy and error codes):
- Missing API key -> friendly CTA with link to Console onboarding
- Fallback used -> return header X-ShortPath-Fallback: true and console hint to reduce batch_size or pin model
- Rate limit -> brief guide: how to configure local quota overrides for dev accounts

Experiment matrix (quick list):
- A/B: initial telemetry sampling 10% vs 50% (measure noise vs usefulness)
- Warmup: enable a 1-request warmup in SDK init (latency vs cost)
- Batch defaults: start 4ms batching window vs immediate send (affects tail latency)
- Cassette retention: store 10 vs 100 snapshots to see CI signal/noise

Acceptance checklist for merging to master: 
- Minimal README with three commands and example screenshots
- shortpath-run binary published to npm/pip test channel
- Scavenger tests added under examples/tests with green CI on PR
- Telemetry events validated against Confluence contract page (link above)
- Quick opt-out toggle (SHORTPATH_DISABLE_RECORD) implemented

Immediate next steps (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Draft README with three-command TL;DR + sample code (due 2025-02-21)
- [ ] Implement stub mode replay endpoint and cassette writer (due 2025-02-28)
- [ ] Wire basic telemetry events to local console output (due 2025-03-04)
- [ ] Create PR skeleton: GH PR #432 is placeholder for implementation branch

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- Cassette privacy: cassettes may contain user prompts. Default should be to redact or require explicit RECORD_CONSENT. How to surface in README?
- Sampling default: 10% feels safe but might be useless for small teams. Should we make it per-org default in Console?
- Should shortpath-run mimic production tokenization exactly (heavy) or approximate (fast)?

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally small and opinionated. The goal is to learn: what minimal surface reduces time-to-success and surfaces production issues quickly. Please focus feedback on friction points in the three-command TL;DR and the scavenger test definitions.

Slack threads / references: #sdk-onramp (thread: "shortpath quickbake") and convo on 2025-02-10 with PMs; see LINEAR-1234 for tracking.

End of notebook.
